category_title: Reserved students who limit participation to interactions with adults
minimal_context: Amber is in an out-of-school biology workshop session looking at a particular set of seed germination bags with her group to determine what can be learned from them.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Everyone, look at this particular set of seed germination bags. What can you learn from them?

STUDENT: (Sits quietly while the group looks at the bags, not blurting ideas out.)

TUTOR: Go ahead and discuss it together with your group.

STUDENT: (Remains reserved, looking at the bags but not speaking to the other students.)

TUTOR: Does anyone have any ideas?

STUDENT: (Continues to stay quiet and reserved, keeping her questions to herself because she does not have the direct attention of an adult.)

options.A: Adjust the rhythm or pace of the workshop session to give the students sufficient time to work over their difficulties and explore the seed germination bags deeply.
options.B: Reposition as a facilitator of instruction, not the ultimate source of knowledge, and allow the students to make sense of the seed germination bags on their own.
options.C: Agree with the student that she is having a rough time with the group activity and the seed germination bags during the workshop session.
options.D: Ask the student a direct question about the seed germination bags and provide immediate positive physical or social reinforcement, such as a high-five.
